key_insight: ConforNets adds a learned latent-control layer to OpenFold3 so the model can reliably and efficiently steer predictions into biologically relevant alternate conformations, rather than returning a single dominant state.
problem_solved: AlphaFold-family models typically output one dominant conformation and inference-time perturbations are ad hoc, inefficient, and inconsistent at recovering major alternative structural modes; this work provides a systematic, trainable mechanism to generate controlled conformational diversity.
method: Integrate a compact latent-control module into OpenFold3 that conditions structure prediction on low-dimensional latent vectors encoding conformational state.
Train the module on structural ensembles or multimodal ground-truth data so latent manipulations map to distinct, biologically meaningful conformations.
Use latent sampling/interpolation at inference time to generate consistent alternative states efficiently (no repeated input perturbations required).
impact: Practitioners gain a scalable, reproducible way to produce plausible conformational ensembles from AlphaFold-style models, improving downstream tasks such as ligand docking, mechanistic hypothesis generation, and structure-based design.
visual_elements: Schematic of OpenFold3 with the ConforNet latent-control module highlighted (showing conditioning pathway).
Before vs after example: single AF prediction contrasted with multiple ConforNets-generated conformations aligned to known experimental states.
Latent-space map (e.g., 2D projection) showing clusters corresponding to distinct conformational modes and arrows for interpolation trajectories.
Performance/efficiency chart comparing recovery rate of major modes and compute time: inference perturbations vs ConforNets.
paper_title: ConforNets: Latents-Based Conformational Control in OpenFold3
paper_authors: Minji Lee, Colin Kalicki, Minkyu Jeon, Aymen Qabel, Alisia Fadini
